issue: Release tests falsely reject a fresh reopened valid document during concurrent model evaluation
actual_failure: Reopening side-hole rejected feature f6, a simple cube Add, as requiring a mesh approximation while another thread executed the known disc-fuse fallback
baseline_serial: Original release tutorial_holes binary passes all three tests with --test-threads=1
cause: Brepkit mesh_fallback_count is process-global; an unrelated Runtime can increment it between a feature snapshot and its exactness check
fix: A process-wide mutex guards each native feature transaction, including execution, exactness/validity checks and rollback. Lock scope is not the whole application or viewport.
panic_behavior: RAII releases the guard during unwinding. Poisoned-lock recovery avoids making future independent evaluations fail.
concurrency: Native feature transactions serialize between Runtime instances in one process. Viewport work and independent processes remain parallel. Direct external calls to Brepkit must not bypass this transaction discipline.
regression: Three synchronized threads, four genuine failing fresh Runtime builds alongside forty valid fresh Runtime builds. Actual failing feature is asserted f6 and previous geometry volume is preserved.

verification.save_load_checks: Every tutorial run saves, loads and freshly regenerates all passing stages, including fillet/chamfer variants
